sources.title: Druze and Alawite leaders endorse decentralized Syria, sparking fierce rebuke from Damascus
North Syria's 'Unity of Communities' conference urges new constitution, decentralized system

stances_toward.note: The alignment of the minorities against Damascus was a 2025 project: the Hasakah 'unity of components' conference (8-9 Aug 2025) heard the Druze leader Sheikh Hikmat al-Hijri and the Alawite sheikh Ghazal Ghazal by video call for a decentralised or federal state and called the SDF a 'necessary nucleus' of a future army; Damascus replied that the conference 'dealt a blow' to talks, held the SDF fully responsible and skipped the Paris round. Druze protesters demonstrated for the SDF in January 2026. Partner, cooling: the alignment never became a military pact and the SDF's integration removed its main instrument; Suwayda has its own track (Israel, Jordan) with Damascus. Bond - affinity (shared minority fear). No source calls it an alliance.

relations_to.summary: 8-9 Aug 2025: the Hasakah 'unity of components' conference hears the Druze leader Sheikh Hikmat al-Hijri and the Alawite sheikh Ghazal Ghazal by video call for a decentralised or federal state; its closing statement names the Autonomous Administration a 'participatory governance model' and the SDF a 'necessary nucleus' of a future army. Damascus says the event 'dealt a blow' to talks, holds the SDF leadership 'fully responsible' and says it will skip the Paris meetings.
